summary: Small world-map cursor record: a vtable word, two cleared header words and five embedded 0x24-byte cursor slots built by std_ConstructArray; the ctor is bracketed by the world-map cursor create/destroy helpers.
evidence: Ui_MapCursor_Ctor (0x0017CD5C) stores the caller vtable in word 0, zeroes words 1-2 and calls std_ConstructArray(cursor+3, 0x00619A8C, 0x24, 5); 5*0x24 + 0xC = 0xC0 (192) bytes, which is larger than the batch's 12-byte max-field estimate. Neighbours are the world-map UI code around 0x0017C910/0x0017CCD8.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ui_MapCursor_Ctor stores arg2 in *cursor (the vtable-in-argument ctor pattern); no other function reads word 0 directly.

fields.name: unknown_04
fields.evidence: Only zero-initialised in Ui_MapCursor_Ctor (cursor[1] = 0); no reader found, purpose unknown.

fields.name: unknown_08
fields.evidence: Only zero-initialised in Ui_MapCursor_Ctor (cursor[2] = 0); the five 0x24-byte cursor slots follow at +0xC.

summary: Cursor-icon container (0x2314 bytes): an embedded cursor at +0 with its intrusive child ring and layout/animation refs, a second cursor at +0x21CC, a helper sub-object at +0x88C and a manager pointer at +0x2310; binds the icon_cursor_default/word2/word3 animations.
evidence: Ui_CursorIcon_BindAnims (0x001D782A) binds 'icon_cursor_default', 'icon_cursor_word2' and 'icon_cursor_word3' into anim refs at +0x4C/+0x9C/+0xEC and ends with a virtual +0x5C call; Ui_CursorIcon_Hide (0x001D7B1C) clears f_50 (+0x140) and calls vtable +0x18 with 1, while FUN_001D7AA0 hides the embedded copy at +0x21CC and uses the manager at +0x2310.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: The deleting/non-deleting dtors (0x001D84CC/0x001D8558) write vtable 0x0075A3E4 here and Ui_CursorIcon_Hide/Show dispatch through slot +0x18.

fields.name: maybe_layoutRoot
fields.evidence: Ui_CursorIcon_BindAnims and maybe_Ui_CursorIcon_RebindWordAnims pass self[1] as the layout argument to Ui_AnimRef_Bind for every cursor animation.

fields.name: maybe_layoutArg

fields.name: maybe_glyphSource
fields.evidence: Ui_CursorIcon_SetWordType calls func_001D806C(self->f_38, buf) to obtain the current glyph cell and then advances the cursor by delta.

fields.name: maybe_cursorParam1
fields.evidence: Read as self[0x15] and forwarded as the third argument of the cursor bind helper; meaning unknown.

fields.name: maybe_cursorParam2

fields.name: maybe_cursorParam3

fields.name: maybe_flag5D
fields.evidence: Read as a char flag in the cursor bind path; no writer or clear meaning found.

fields.name: unknown_60
fields.evidence: Batch evidence is a virtual dispatch through *self slot +0x18 (hide/show), not a direct +0x60 access; the offset is unexplained.

fields.name: maybe_animRef
fields.evidence: The dtors at 0x001D84CC/0x001D8558 call Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self + 0x19) with self as u32*, i.e. the embedded layout/animation ref at +0x64.

fields.name: maybe_wordType
fields.evidence: A setter stores its char argument in byte +0x6F and compares it with 1 to select the word cursor; BindAnims keeps a 3-entry active-word byte at +0x13C, so this is the per-word selector.

fields.name: maybe_childRingHead
fields.evidence: The dtors walk the intrusive ring starting at self[0x2D] (+0xB4) until it reaches self[0x2E] and re-link it afterwards; +0xB4 is the ring's sentinel/head.

fields.name: maybe_childRingFirst

fields.name: maybe_childRingLast

fields.name: isVisible
fields.evidence: Ui_CursorIcon_Hide writes 0 to f_50 (+0x140) right before hiding the pane; its Show counterpart (0x001D7B54) clears the hide state again.

fields.name: owner
fields.evidence: Hide/Show dereference self[0x51] (+0x144) and call vtable slots +0x10/+0x14 on it to play the cursor animation, so it is the owning render/layout object.

fields.name: maybe_subCursorA
fields.evidence: FUN_001D7AA0 calls FUN_00259928(self, self + 0x88C), i.e. +0x88C is the base of an embedded sub-object reset on close.

summary: 40-slot hit/attack icon board: a shared float timer plus an array of 0x28 slots of 0xC bytes {target object, 'icon_*' pane, is-hit flag}; the per-frame update rebuilds the 'icon_atari' highlight.
evidence: Ui_HitIcon_Ctor (0x00446978) chains Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x0076FF44 and zero-fills 0x1E0 bytes at +0x58; Ui_HitIcon_Add (0x00446798) and Ui_HitIcon_Update (0x00445DBC) walk exactly 0x28 slots from +0x58 to +0x238 in 0xC-byte steps.

fields.name: timer
fields.evidence: Ui_HitIcon_Update computes self->f_50 - self->f_54, stores it back and wraps it using the global frame delta, i.e. an accumulating effect timer.

fields.name: timerStep
fields.evidence: Subtracted from the timer every update; the ctor preloads it with 0xC483C000 (a negative float) so the timer counts up.

fields.name: slots
fields.evidence: Start of the 0x28-entry array: Ui_HitIcon_Add iterates (int*)(self+0x58) to (int*)(self+0x238) in 3-word steps and writes {target, pane, isHit} into a free slot; Ui_HitIcon_ClearAllSlots does the same.

fields.name: maybe_slotsEnd
fields.evidence: Loop bound in Ui_HitIcon_Add/Update/ClearAllSlots, equal to +0x58 + 0x28*0xC; it is the end of the slot array rather than a stored field.

fields.name: maybe_iconObject

fields.name: unknown_120
fields.evidence: Batch evidence is a virtual dispatch through *self slot +0x48; no direct +0x120 access was found, so the offset is unexplained.

fields.name: maybe_slotTable
fields.evidence: Four 0x14-byte callback descriptors start at +0xA20 (raw self+0x288 with self as int*); each holds an object pointer, a record callback and an update callback, and the loop runs until +0xB60.

fields.name: slotsRegistered
fields.evidence: maybe_Ui_NpcIcon_UpdateFromRecord tests byte +0xB60 (raw self[0x2D8]) so the four slots are registered only once, then sets it to 1.

summary: Status-effect icon widget (1232 bytes): an embedded six-row count list and a pane at +0x4A4 whose atlas texture is selected from a command record type (textures 0x83..0x9B).
evidence: maybe_Ui_StatusIcon_SetFromType (0x002FC280) calls Ui_SixRowCountList_SetEntries on &self->f_2F8, a part animation helper, then sets the pane at &self->f_4A4 using (u32)self->f_4CC << 0x10 and texture 0x83+type when type < 0x19.

fields.name: countList
fields.evidence: Ui_SixRowCountList_SetEntries(&self->f_2F8) is the first call of maybe_Ui_StatusIcon_SetFromType, so +0x2F8 is the embedded count-list object.

fields.name: maybe_iconPane
fields.evidence: func_001A6680(&self->f_4A4, (u32)self->f_4CC << 0x10, texture) sets the icon pane/texture; the 4-byte value is the pane handle.

fields.name: frameIndex
fields.evidence: The u16 at +0x4CC is shifted left 16 and OR-ed into the pane id passed to func_001A6680, i.e. the pane/texture frame index.

summary: Tiny (8-byte) quest-marker record returned by the three Ui_QuestIcon_Create* factories: {pane, actor handle, ..., update callback}; it is stored in the map-icon descriptor table, not a standalone object with methods.
evidence: Ui_QuestIcon_CreateA/B (0x00291FC4/0x002920E4) fill out[0] = created 'icon_anpc_quest.bflyt' pane, out[1] = handle, out[3] = position callback and out[4] = heading callback; the only 'field' at +4 is the factory record's handle word/table tag and +0x92A60 is a game-work offset mistyped as a self field.

fields.name: unknown_04
fields.evidence: All evidence for +4 is the handle-table tag word at 0x007B80C0 entry[1] (piVar2[1] == handle >> 0xB), which is not a member of this 8-byte record; the real second record word (out[1], the actor handle) has no verified type.

fields.name: unknown_92A60
fields.evidence: Single 'weak' access: FUN_0066AF08(*piVar2 + 0x24A98, cVar1) is the game-work bag offset, i.e. the decompiler mistyped the game-work pointer as a field of Ui_QuestIcon; ignore it for layout.

summary: Small icon widget (44 bytes): a single pane/texture slot whose atlas frame is selected from a type code (type < 0x19 -> texture 0x83+type, otherwise empty).
evidence: Ui_Icon_SetFromType (0x002FC2B8) calls func_00633560(atlas, type+0x83) and then func_001A6680(self, (u32)self->f_28 << 0x10, texture), i.e. +0x28 is the pane/frame index.

fields.name: frameIndex
fields.evidence: The u16 at +0x28 is shifted left 16 into the pane id passed to func_001A6680 for both the textured and the empty case.

summary: Item icon widget (100 bytes): shows an item's icon and the 'no item' overlay by setting the two panes through the item-record fields; no verified data member beyond its inherited object header.
evidence: Ui_ItemIcon_SetFromItem (0x00409E80) only reads the item record (flag byte, icon frame) and calls the show/hide virtual slot +0x18 plus func_001A6680; the only batch offset +0x60 comes from that virtual dispatch, not from a stored member.

summary: World-map ship marker (2292 bytes): lazily creates the 'icon_aship2.bflyt' sprite once and drives its position from the vehicle record each frame.
evidence: Ui_MapShipIcon_Update (0x003A7C4C) loads f_8F0, creates the sprite with func_003A7B38(self, 'icon_aship2.bflyt') when zero and caches it, then copies the position triple into the sprite's +0x1C/+0x20/+0x24.

fields.name: shipSprite
fields.evidence: Lazily created once in Ui_MapShipIcon_Update and reused; the sprite pane receives the ship position and the +0x44 draw flag is set.

summary: Sprite/text draw record (344 bytes): owns three embedded draw targets, a selected render node, a layer word and an embedded parameter block at +0xFC that is applied to the lyt node (size, character code, colours, flip flags).
evidence: Ui_Sprite_Draw (0x002283FC) selects one of three draw targets from f_C (0/2) and the record flags (+0x14 / +0x18 / +0x1C) and dispatches vtable slots +8/+0x10/+0x18; Ui_Sprite_ApplyParams (0x002D0E98) applies the block at +0xFC (size f_20/f_22, char code f_2C, colours f_14/f_2E/f_30/f_33/f_34) to the node at +0xC; Ui_Sprite_AttachToLayer/DetachFromLayer store the layer at +0x44.

fields.name: renderNode
fields.evidence: Ui_Sprite_ApplyParams writes self->f_C->f_77/f_60/f_6D/f_73/f_78/f_7A and calls Text_SetCharCode/Ui_SpriteTree_ApplyLayout on self->f_C, i.e. the attached lyt sprite node; Ui_Sprite_Draw switches on f_C's mode 0/2.

fields.name: maybe_nodeFlags

fields.name: drawTarget
fields.evidence: Ui_Sprite_Draw stores the chosen target pointer (one of the embedded targets or the owner's +0x11C) into self->f_10 and dispatches vtable +8/+0x10 through it.

fields.name: maybe_drawFlags
fields.evidence: The byte at +0x11 is copied into the node's +0x48; the node field's meaning is unknown.

fields.name: maybe_ownerObject
fields.evidence: Ui_Sprite_Draw uses self->f_14 when the record's flip/vis flag is 0 and takes &f_14->f_11C as the draw target, so it points at an owner object whose +0x11C is a pane.

fields.name: maybe_paramByte
fields.evidence: Copied to the node's +0x77 by Ui_Sprite_ApplyParams; not enough evidence for a name.

fields.name: maybe_drawTargetB
fields.evidence: Ui_Sprite_Draw takes &self->f_18 as a draw target and calls its vtable slot +0x18, so +0x18 is an embedded polymorphic draw target; ApplyParams separately copies word +0x18 into node+0x60.

fields.name: maybe_drawTargetC

fields.name: width
fields.evidence: Ui_Sprite_ApplyParams passes (int)self->f_20 and (int)self->f_22 to func_0029E740, the node size setter, i.e. width and height of the quad.

fields.name: height

fields.name: alpha

fields.name: charCode

fields.name: maybe_fontStyle

fields.name: maybe_palette

summary: Cursor sprite widget: a two-part 'cursor_base'/'cursor_select' sprite plus a number animation whose current state and frame counter are cached in the object.
evidence: Ui_CursorSprite_Init (0x004DC6C0) plays 'cursor_base'/'cursor_select' and calls Ui_CursorSprite_PlayNumberAnim(self,0); Ui_CursorSprite_PlayNumberAnim (0x004DC610) plays 'num_loop'/'num_out'/'num_in' into f_EC and caches the state in f_F0, resetting f_F4.

fields.name: numberAnim

fields.name: animState

fields.name: maybe_animFrame
